title: Karazhan: The Master’s Key and Nightbane
summary: Alturus’s investigation leads Khadgar to restore a key divided across Outland. A separate Violet Eye search for Medivh’s Journal uncovers a memory of Arcanagos and a ritual that raises Nightbane.
opening: A tower in Deadwind Pass has sealed itself away, and the Violet Eye’s reading finds a faint demonic echo. The road to reopen Karazhan crosses Outland; the later search for Medivh’s Journal begins a separate inquiry into what the tower remembers.

chapters.title: Restore the Master’s Key
chapters.body:
Below Karazhan, Archmage Alturus watched a tower whose doors had closed against the world. The Violet Eye sought answers among arcane disturbances and restless dead. Beneath the tower and around its grounds, the investigation began along separate paths. An old place had withdrawn into silence, leaving those outside to discover what troubled it and what had become of the people within.

Alturus gave the seeker a Violet Scrying Crystal to read the underground waters of the Master’s Cellar. The result troubled him. Where arcane currents should have flowed, he found a vast energy vacuum and only a faint demonic echo. The cellar had yielded a warning without naming the presence behind it. Above, Karazhan remained closed.

Alturus’s report reached Archmage Cedric in Dalaran’s old crater. Cedric knew the tower had sealed itself, and that the Violet Eye had lost contact with agents inside. The strange reading deepened that silence. He pointed toward Khadgar, Medivh’s former apprentice, now in Shattrath. Someone who remembered the tower’s master might know how its door could be opened.

In Shattrath, Khadgar received the report and recognized a familiar difficulty. Karazhan could not simply be forced open. The Master’s Key had once held that power, and he knew its history. He agreed to help restore it. The way back to the old tower would first pass through Outland’s changed strongholds, seeking what he had left there in another time.

While stranded in Outland, Khadgar had divided his key into three fragments and hidden them in enchanted containers. Their resting places had seemed safe then. The broken world had changed since, and each refuge now bore other dangers. To restore the key, the seeker would have to recover its pieces from places no longer sheltered as their keeper remembered them.

One fragment waited in the Shadow Labyrinth, among passages occupied by the Shadow Council. Khadgar had once trusted that hiding place. Its recovery brought a part of the key out of his memory and into the seeker’s hands. Yet Karazhan’s door remained beyond reach. Elsewhere in Outland, two more fragments lay within strongholds changed by time and occupation.

Another container was recovered in the Steamvault beneath Coilfang Reservoir. Khadgar had hidden it under Serpent Lake before the place bore that name. He suspected the naga’s great drain had carried it into the reservoir. Whatever course the waters had given it, the fragment was found. A changed landscape had yielded another part of the old key.

The last fragment lay in the Arcatraz, a prison within Tempest Keep. Khadgar had hidden it when the naaru held the fortress. Now Kael’thas’s forces had turned the vessel into a place of confinement. From a refuge made dangerous, the seeker recovered the final piece. All three could return to the man who had divided them.

Khadgar restored the key, but it still required Medivh’s consent. Through time, the seeker entered the Black Morass at the Opening of the Dark Portal. Medivh recognized the key as Khadgar’s, though he had not yet given it to his apprentice. Within that remembered past, the restored object received the permission its keeper could not grant for himself.

The key returned to Khadgar in Shattrath. A way into Karazhan now existed. Across changed strongholds and a memory of the past, the seeker had restored the means of entry. Yet an open door could not explain the tower’s silence or the fate of its investigators. Those questions remained with the Violet Eye, waiting beyond the threshold.

chapters.title: The Journal and its Memory
chapters.body:
Within Karazhan, another Violet Eye inquiry sought Medivh’s Journal. Alturus’s earlier agents had not returned; Wravien was the last named seeker. The tower linked this search to the work that had opened its door, but the lost book carried a burden of its own. Among halls rich with knowledge, the investigators hoped to recover a memory of the Guardian himself.

In the Guardian’s Library, Wravien struggled to remember his commission. He directed the seeker to Gradav, whose own work held him fast; Gradav pointed onward to Kamsis. Each offered part of the way, yet none could simply lead the search to its end. The library’s abundance had become an obstacle, and the lost investigators remained caught within their confusion and fixation.

Kamsis directed the seeker toward the Shade of Aran, Medivh’s father. When the shade was overcome, the Journal was recovered. A search for a lost book had reached the chance to witness what its pages preserved. Within Karazhan’s guarded knowledge waited one of Medivh’s own memories, bearing a danger older than the Violet Eye’s present inquiry.

On the Master’s Terrace, the Journal opened upon an older meeting. Arcanagos, a blue dragon, warned Medivh that a dark power sought to use him and urged him to leave. Medivh refused. Magic burned through the dragon from within, and Arcanagos fled aflame. The memory closed upon a terrible act whose remains might still carry part of its meaning.

chapters.title: From Charred Bone to Nightbane
chapters.body:
Alturus wondered whether Medivh had woven some of his essence into the magic that defeated Arcanagos. Perhaps a trace endured in the dragon’s bones. The seeker searched the mountains south of Karazhan and recovered a charred fragment. It was a beginning for the archmage’s inquiry, carrying the possibility of an answer without yet proving what the old magic had left behind.

The bone was sent to Kalynna Lathred in Area 52. Once of the Kirin Tor, she now pursued studies her old order forbade. Alturus called the fragment’s essence lifeless, like Arcanagos himself. Kalynna believed she could help, but asked a price. The Violet Eye’s question had reached a scholar whose boundaries differed from those of the order she had left.

Kalynna demanded two books before completing the favor. Nethekurse held the Tome of Dusk in the Shattered Halls; Darkweaver Syth held the Book of Forgotten Names in Sethekk Halls. Separate journeys brought the volumes within reach. The bargain joined forbidden study to the search for Medivh’s lingering essence, preparing the means to call forth what remained of the dragon.

On the Master’s Terrace, Kalynna’s materials were set alight within a Blackened Urn. The released energy raised Arcanagos’s charred remains as Nightbane. The adventurer defeated him and carried his essence to Alturus. The old memory had yielded a sample, but no full explanation of the Guardian’s power. Above Karazhan, the inquiry ended with an answer still waiting to be understood.

reviewNote: Complete 18-scene illustrated research story with transcript-matched AI narration, source and claim records, dedicated TBC-area art, distinct principal cast, and pivotal key, journal, bone and urn illustrations. The Master’s Key and Nightbane quest chains are separate and joined editorially at Karazhan; historical travel through the Black Morass and journal memories are explicitly labeled. Target evidence: The Burning Crusade original 2.0.3–2.4.3 quest era, before Wrath-era changes; current accessible references include Blizzard’s TBC Classic overview and secondary reproductions. Original-client/build and exact quest-dialogue capture, chronology, Atiesh scene/model comparison, area-resemblance review, source approval, and narration audition remain open. No Legion Return to Karazhan or later character outcomes are included.
